headline: Amazon's cloud arm has promised another $1 billion over five years to the towns where it builds data centers, as local opposition to those centers grows.
score_reason: A $1 billion pledge by a major cloud company answering growing local opposition; it is a promise, not yet spending, so the pool score is kept.
importance_line: It is aimed at people living near Amazon's data centers, but it is a company pledge, and the opposition CBS describes centers on worries about harm to the environment and local resources.
summary: CBS News reports that Amazon Web Services, Amazon's cloud-computing arm, announced on 2 Oct 2026 that it will spend an additional $1 billion over five years in the communities that host its data centers, on top of earlier commitments, for education, job training, keeping energy affordable, saving water and energy, and other local needs. AWS chief executive Matt Garman said in a blog post that a lapse in national focus could put the US behind in the AI race, while a CBS poll found more Americans oppose than favor data centers in their own area.
